mission: PBUF FND-002 Justification of the Microscopic State

assumption_audit.assumption: Exactly three microscopic degrees of freedom
assumption_audit.label: NEW POSTULATE
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: Yes: CORE-001 calls it an existing PBUF working premise, while explicitly saying it is not derived.
assumption_audit.derivable: No; neither the supplied equations nor symmetry data select dim(q)=3.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: require only a microscopic state with at least one matter-coupled projection.
assumption_audit.remove: From the scalar closure, yes; from the stated three-degree PBUF ontology, no.
assumption_audit.observable: Extra components matter only if they have distinct sources, modes, or couplings; the frozen laboratory observes one projection.
assumption_audit.changed: CORE-001 internal O(3) interpretation changes, but its scalar long-wave equation need not.

assumption_audit.label: NEW POSTULATE
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: Yes: CORE-001 identifies 1/137 as an existing characteristic-scale premise, not a derivation.
assumption_audit.derivable: No. Corrected CORE-001 places g_dev directly in the normalized matter vertex; its numerical value remains a PBUF premise rather than a consequence of the other assumptions.
assumption_audit.weaken: No within the stated PBUF ontology: replacing g_dev by an effective coefficient would discard the fundamental-coupling premise.
assumption_audit.remove: No without removing the stated PBUF matter coupling; the zero-coupling limit removes matter loading.
assumption_audit.observable: The normalized microscopic source and conditional coarse source scale directly with g_dev; downstream observability still requires response and access maps.
assumption_audit.changed: The former source-normalization degeneracy is withdrawn; lack of a derivation of the numerical value remains.

assumption_audit.label: OPTIONAL
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: No earlier supplied material requires a lattice; CORE-001 introduced it as a regulator.
assumption_audit.derivable: No specific regulator is derivable. Isotropic leading-order propagation follows conditionally from spatial rotational symmetry.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: any statistically homogeneous, isotropic local substrate with a valid long-wave limit suffices.
assumption_audit.remove: Yes: a continuum microfield or isotropic graph Laplacian gives the same effective operator.
assumption_audit.observable: Finite-spacing anisotropy and dispersion can appear beyond the long-wave regime.
assumption_audit.changed: Only regulator-level corrections change if the same isotropic continuum limit is retained.

assumption_audit.label: OPTIONAL
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: No quantitative matter-state law exists in the supplied pre-CORE material.
assumption_audit.derivable: Only as the first Taylor term of an analytic interaction about a reference state, assuming a nonzero linear coefficient.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: require a differentiable local source whose leading perturbative term is linear.
assumption_audit.remove: Yes, but a purely nonlinear source changes the weak-loading closure.
assumption_audit.observable: It fixes superposition and leading response to density; nonlinear terms create amplitude-dependent response.
assumption_audit.changed: The exact Helmholtz form and density scaling generally cease to hold outside the linearized regime.

assumption_audit.label: DERIVED
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: CORE-001 defines it; earlier material asks for stiffness/recovery but does not fix the potential.
assumption_audit.derivable: Yes as the universal leading nonconstant term of a smooth stable energy expanded about a nondegenerate equilibrium.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: assume only smoothness, stability, and positive Hessian at equilibrium.
assumption_audit.remove: The exact quadratic model can be removed; some stabilizing recovery is required for finite static susceptibility.
assumption_audit.observable: Leading response is linear; higher powers produce nonlinear saturation away from equilibrium.
assumption_audit.changed: Without positive local curvature the unloaded state may be unstable or the Helmholtz mass term vanishes.

assumption_audit.label: OPTIONAL
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: No; it is a CORE-001 discretization choice.
assumption_audit.derivable: No. A gradient-squared term is the leading local isotropic spatial correction, but many microscopic couplings generate it.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: finite-range or sufficiently decaying, symmetric couplings with a finite second moment.
assumption_audit.remove: Yes: graph, nonlocal, or direct continuum operators may share the same small-wavenumber expansion.
assumption_audit.observable: Higher-order dispersion and short-scale propagation depend on the coupling stencil.
assumption_audit.changed: Long-wave G is renormalized; nonlocal tails or anisotropy can change the continuum operator itself.

assumption_audit.label: OPTIONAL
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: No supplied theory selects first-order time evolution; CORE-001 chose it for static relaxation.
assumption_audit.derivable: No. The static Euler-Lagrange equation is independent of whether relaxation is overdamped, inertial, or otherwise equilibrating.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: require dynamics that converge to stationary extrema of the effective energy.
assumption_audit.remove: Yes for the static milestone and frozen laboratory.
assumption_audit.observable: Transient response, mode spectrum, causality, and damping differ.
assumption_audit.changed: Nothing static if the same equilibrium is reached; time-dependent predictions change completely.

assumption_audit.label: OPTIONAL
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: Coarse graining is required by CORE-001, but no supplied PBUF source fixes a kernel.
assumption_audit.derivable: No unique kernel. Normalization and symmetry constraints follow from preserving constants and rotations.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: any normalized, localized operator with vanishing first moment and controlled higher moments.
assumption_audit.remove: A distinct kernel can be removed in a direct continuum formulation; a scale-separation map remains conceptually necessary for discrete models.
assumption_audit.observable: Kernel moments control smoothing and finite-resolution corrections, not the leading constant/slow-field limit.
assumption_audit.changed: A nonnormalized or biased kernel fails constant preservation; anisotropic kernels imprint directional artifacts.

assumption_audit.label: SUPPORTED
assumption_audit.explicit_in_pbuf: Yes at the existing continuum/frozen-laboratory interface; earlier discovery material still lists scalar versus tensor character as open microscopically.
assumption_audit.derivable: No fundamental scalar ontology follows. A scalar effective field follows conditionally when the laboratory couples to one invariant projection and other modes decouple.
assumption_audit.weaken: Yes: u may be the scalar observable sector of vector or tensor internal states.
assumption_audit.remove: Not without changing the frozen laboratory interface; it can be emergent rather than fundamental.
assumption_audit.observable: Additional unsuppressed tensor/vector sectors would generate responses absent from a single scalar field.
assumption_audit.changed: The current constitutive and gradient interfaces require revision if extra continuum modes couple appreciably.

minimal_postulates: P1: A microscopic PBUF state exists and admits a stable, approximately local, rotationally invariant long-wavelength sector.
P2: Matter sources at least one dimensionless scalar observable sector u; other microscopic components are absent, massive, or decoupled at laboratory scales.
P3: The effective static response has positive finite local susceptibility and a positive leading spatial stiffness.

P4: PBUF's exactly-three-state and characteristic-1/137 statements are retained as ontology premises, but existing material supplies no derivation and the scalar closure cannot identify them separately.
